Collections operations and the conduct rulebook

After this lesson you can:
  • Design a bucket-based collections strategy with treatments and channels
  • State the conduct rules: contact hours, harassment prohibition, agent notice
  • Explain PTP discipline and field/cash controls

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Strategy: right treatment, right account
  2. The conduct rulebook is law, not etiquette
  3. Field and cash: the leakiest pipe, plumbed
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS

1. Strategy: right treatment, right account

Collections is segmentation.

Strategy assigns each account a treatment plan by product, bucket, risk and history: soft reminders (SMS/WhatsApp/email) in early buckets, telecalling with trained scripts as delinquency deepens, field visits and agency placement for hard buckets, legal review beyond that.

The workhorse metric is the PTP — promise to pay: a dated commitment, tracked kept-or-broken, with broken promises escalating the treatment.

Vulnerable customers (hardship, illness, disaster) get differentiated handling — module 6's resolution lesson covers where hardship legitimately leads.

2. The conduct rulebook is law, not etiquette

India's collections conduct rules — Fair Practices Code, Digital Lending Directions, outsourcing directions — are explicit:

  • Contact hours — no calls or visits outside the permitted window (broadly 8:00–19:00 under conduct guidance); LoanOS encodes this as a contact-hours guard on reminder and notice logging.
  • No harassment — no abuse, intimidation, public shaming, contacting the borrower's contact list. The app-lending scandals that produced the 2021–22 crackdown were precisely these behaviours.
  • Agent accountability — recovery agents are registered, due-diligenced and trained; the borrower is notified before an agent makes contact, with the agent's identity; complaints against agents are tracked and can suspend them.
  • RE liability — every one of these failures by an outsourced agency lands on the RE (module 1's non-transferable accountability).

For a BA, each rule is a system control: a dialer that ignores contact hours, or an agent assignment without borrower notice, is a build defect with regulatory consequences.

3. Field and cash: the leakiest pipe, plumbed

Field collection handles the cash economy: visits with geo/time evidence, digital receipts issued on the spot, and the platform's rule that cash collected posts to the account the same day — the gap between collection and posting is where fraud lives. Cash exceptions require approval; agency settlements (fees, incentives) reconcile against evidenced collections.

LoanOS ships an Android field-operations app for exactly this workflow — visits, receipts, evidence — feeding the same ledger and audit chain as every other channel.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Recovery conduct, agent-notice duty and borrower protection in digital lending.
  • RBI-OUTSOURCE — Agency conduct is the RE's responsibility; due diligence and review are mandatory.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability CLL-004 — Reminder and notice logging with contact-hours guard.
  • Capability CLL-006 — Promise-to-pay, kept/broken PTP and follow-up.
  • Capability CLL-007 — Recovery-agent registry, due diligence and authorization.

  • Capability CLL-011 — Cash exception approval and same-day account posting.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. A dialer campaign is configured to start at 7:00 am 'to catch borrowers before work'. What should block it?

  1. Nothing — mornings are efficient
  2. The contact-hours guard: calls outside the permitted window violate conduct rules
  3. Telecom regulations only
  4. Borrower preferences only
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Contact-hour limits are conduct law under FPC/DLD guidance; LoanOS encodes the window as a guard on outreach logging.

2. Before a recovery agent first contacts a borrower, what must exist?

  1. A court order
  2. Borrower notification of the assignment and the agent's identity
  3. An NPA classification
  4. A settlement offer
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Advance notice of agent assignment is a regulatory duty; LoanOS implements it as a blocking control (CLL-008).
